angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 530,123 km at 45.74 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.8635 +/- 0.0193 mas (same row, RUWE 1.15): 45.74 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.762 +/- 0.005 solar radii from Tuson et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 15906 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523.3090T/abstract): 530,123 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.79 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Tuson et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 15906 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523.3090T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4757 +/- 89 K from Tuson et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 15906 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523.3090T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Tuson et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 15906 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523.3090T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-15906.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.572, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
